title: Pollo alla Cacciatora
subtitle: Hunter's chicken with tomatoes and olives
excerpt: Bone-in chicken pieces braised in tomato, white wine, capers, and olives. A classic of Italian home cooking, it takes about an hour and is even better the next day.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pollo alla cacciatora (hunter's chicken) is one of the most widespread Italian braised chicken dishes, with variations across every region. The combination of tomato, olives, capers, and white wine is typical of the Roman and Tuscan versions.

recipeTools.notes: Wide enough to fit all the chicken pieces in a single layer.

content.text: Cacciatora is bone-in chicken braised in a tomato sauce with white wine, capers, and olives. The chicken gives the sauce body as it cooks, and the capers and olives cut through the richness. It tastes better made ahead and reheated, once the flavours have settled.

Season the chicken pieces with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a large dutch oven over a medium-high heat. Brown the chicken on all sides in batches, about 4 minutes per batch. Lift out and set aside.
Reduce the heat to medium. Add the onion and red pepper. Cook for 6 minutes. Add the garlic and rosemary and cook for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and let it bubble for 2 minutes, scraping the base. Add the tomatoes, olives, and capers. Stir together and return the chicken to the pot, skin-side up.
Bring to a gentle simmer, cover, and cook for 40 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and tender. For the last 10 minutes, remove the lid to let the sauce reduce and thicken.
Remove the rosemary sprigs. Taste for seasoning. Scatter over the parsley and serve.
